physicalNotes: Radius: KELT-9 is a rapid rotator. Ahlers et al. (2020, AJ 160, 4; arXiv:2004.14812) fit its TESS transit with a gravity-darkened oblate star: equatorial radius 2.39 +/- 0.03 solar radii (Table 2) and an equatorial radius 1.089 +/- 0.017 times the polar radius (abstract), so a polar radius of 2.1947. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, (2.39^2 x 2.1947)^(1/3) = 2.3230 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius; the scene draws the flattening, with the equatorial radius on the outline. GM from the stellar mass 2.52 +0.25/-0.20 solar masses (Gaudi et al. 2017, Nature 546, 514, Extended Data Table 3, adopted Model 1, which Ahlers et al. adopt) times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: the display axis, the spin axis measured against KELT-9b's orbit, is up.
